sights.name: Sakyo Cape
sights.description: Scenic point at the tip of Yahata Peninsula, with about 1km of cliffs and columnar basalt rocks called Kannon Pillars.

sights.name: Tsukuyomi Shrine
sights.description: Quiet forest shrine to Tsukuyomi, said to hear wishes about the calendar, tides, safety, and safe navigation.

sights.description: 110m-around natural hole in Makizaki Park, legendarily an ogre's footprint, chosen among Japan's 100 famous caves in 2013.

sights.name: Kumano Shrine
sights.description: Identified with Kii's Kumano Shrine. Tachibana Sadakane is recorded as enshrining it after praying in Empress Jingu's Silla campaign.

sights.name: Katsumoto Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins on a hill overlooking Katsumoto Port and Tsushima, said built in four months in 1591 for Hideyoshi.

sights.name: Otake Shrine
sights.description: Shrine where the whole mountain was once off-limits, said to be where Iki's first gods descended, enshrining Sarutahiko.

sights.name: Kakegi Kofun
sights.description: Round tumulus from the late 6th to early 7th century, retaining Iki's only hollowed house-shaped stone coffin.

sights.name: Amatenagao Shrine
sights.description: Iki's first shrine atop 137 mossy steps. Its 1070 Maitreya is Japan's third-oldest stone statue, an Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Iki Foundation Stone
sights.description: Cliffs of Katsumoto Formation at Amagahara Coast: sandstone and mudstone laid down about 25 million years ago, Iki's oldest strata.

sights.name: Matsunaga Memorial Museum
sights.description: Memorial museum for Iki-born Yasuzaemon Matsunaga, showing his belongings, letters, and a 1909 Fukuoka streetcar at the entrance.

sights.name: Haruichiban Tower
sights.description: Ship-shaped tower erected in 1987 at Motoi Park to remember fishermen lost in the strong 1859 south wind.

sights.name: Haze Rock Dike
sights.description: About 40 m dike on southern Iki, locally called Shirataki, where black basalt rises through white rhyolite. Prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Sugoroku Kofun
sights.description: Nagasaki's largest keyhole tumulus, 91m long on a 100m hill, with a gondola-shaped boat carving in the stone chamber.

sights.name: Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Formerly Kairi Hachiman Shrine; records Iki whaling's start. Peach-shaped basin; elephants and pigeons carved on vermilion hall.

sights.name: Tsushimazuka Kofun
sights.description: National historic site, Iki's second-largest keyhole tumulus at 63m, with geometric and triangular carvings in the stone chamber.

sights.name: Mitarashimizu Falls
sights.description: Falls said to have formed when Kobo Daishi struck a rock with his staff.

sights.name: Hime Shrine / Tobikawa Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Emperor Jimmu and three other deities. Annual festival is April 3 with a procession and ritual dance.

sights.name: Hyozu Shrine
sights.description: Priest is not resident; reserve a shrine stamp by phone. Enshrines Susanoo, Onamuchi, and Kotoshironushi.

sights.name: Kokubunji Temple Ruins

sights.name: Misakito Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 811; enshrines Yamato Takeru. One of 24 Engishiki shrines. Guardian lions said to be by Yamauchi Rihei.

sights.name: Shichiro Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Susanoo and four other deities. The annual festival is November 28, with a ritual dance.

sights.name: Ashibe Sumiyoshi Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Amaterasu and five other deities. The annual festival falls on the 9th day of the 9th lunar month.

sights.name: Kuraokami Shrine
sights.description: Annual festival on the 20th of the 9th lunar month includes a procession and ritual dance.

sights.name: Seibo Shrine

sights.name: Grave of Shoni Suketoki

sights.name: Ikeda Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Emperor Ojin. Annual festival is November 21 with ritual dance; deity-welcoming rite is November 29.

sights.name: Kagamitake Shrine
sights.description: The hall is on the summit, reached by over 300 stone steps with large rises; climb slowly and carefully.

sights.name: Ankoku-ji
sights.description: Rinzai temple renamed from Kaiin-ji in 1338. Holds an Important Cultural Property sutra and a cedar over 600 years.

sights.name: Kunitsuokami Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Susanoo. Guardian lions by Iki master Yamauchi Rihei, made in 1862 at 63, have small heads and gentle form.

sights.name: Takamioya Shrine
sights.description: Said to date from 811. Enshrines Takamimusubi, Izanagi, and Izanami, with two rare pairs of guardian lions in the grounds.

sights.name: Fukae Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Izanami and Okunitama. Annual festival is November 11 with a procession and ritual dance.

sights.name: Kifune Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Takaokami. The annual festival includes an offering rite and a procession.

sights.name: Kurosaki Battery Ruins
sights.description: Huge battery ruins near Saruiwa, completed in 1933 with two 41cm cannons using main guns from the battleship Akagi.

sights.name: Sui Shrine
sights.description: One of Iki's 24 Engishiki shrines. Enshrines Hayaakitsuhi and Sugawara Michizane. Annual festival is November 25.

sights.name: Togami Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Susanoo and two other deities. Annual festival is October 26, with a procession and ritual dance.

sights.name: Iki Shrine

sights.name: Ishida Tenman Shrine

activities.name: Motomiya Park

sights.name: Dejima
sights.description: Japan's only window to the West during isolation; restored buildings and materials are open to many visitors.

sights.name: Peace Park (Peace Statue and Fountain of Peace)
sights.description: Prayer space for atomic bomb victims and lasting peace. A peace ceremony is held before the statue on August 9.

sights.name: Hashima (Battleship Island)
sights.description: Sunday-drama setting. Supported Japan's modernization as an undersea coal-mine island; closed in 1974.

sights.name: Mount Inasa
sights.description: Nagasaki landmark with the ten-million-dollar night view, one of Japan's new three great night views.

sights.name: Spectacles Bridge
sights.description: Said to be built in 1634; partly collapsed in the 1982 flood, restored, and a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Oura Cathedral
sights.description: Japan's oldest existing church, a Gothic building for foreign residents, dedicated to the 26 martyrs.

sights.name: Dutch Slope
sights.description: Stone-paved slope in Higashiyamate, lined with Western-style houses full of exotic atmosphere.

sights.name: Glover Garden
sights.description: Hilltop garden of Meiji Western houses, including the Former Glover House, overlooking Nagasaki Port.

sights.name: One-Pillar Torii (Sanno Shrine)
sights.description: Sanno Shrine stands about 800m southeast of the hypocenter and was damaged in August 1945. One original torii remains.

sights.name: Sofuku-ji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1629 by Chinese monk Chozen and called Fuzhou Temple; two buildings are National Treasures.

sights.name: Peace Park (Atomic Bomb Hypocenter)
sights.description: Black granite marks where the bomb burst about 500m above Matsuyama-machi at 11:02 on August 9, 1945. Melted glass remains.

sights.name: Nagasaki Penguin Aquarium
sights.description: Aquarium keeping nine of 18 penguin species, about 180 birds, over 70 percent born here.

sights.name: Nabekaburiyama Park
sights.description: 169m park whose 2016 observatory overlooks Nagasaki Port, the city, and mortar-shaped terrain.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Kameyama Shachu Memorial Museum
sights.description: Group founded in 1865 by Ryoma Sakamoto and comrades, called Japan's first trading company.

sights.name: Chinzei Taisha Suwa Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1625 and called Osuwa-san; Kunchi dances are a national Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property.

sights.name: Tojin Yashiki Ruins
sights.description: Site of the 1689 Chinese quarter built to confine residents; a symbolic gate stands now.

sights.name: Shianbashi
sights.description: Bridge near Maruyama named because people hesitated over entering the costly pleasure quarter.

sights.name: Shiroyama Elementary School Peace Memorial Hall
sights.description: Preserved stair tower of the school about 500 meters west of the hypocenter, where over 1,400 died.

sights.name: Kofuku-ji Temple
sights.description: Japan's first Chinese temple and birthplace of the Obaku sect, founded in 1620 by Nanjing Chinese.

sights.name: Nyoko-do
sights.description: Two-mat sickroom and study beside the Nagai Memorial Hall, built for Dr. Takashi Nagai, who wrote there while battling leukemia.

sights.name: Yamazato Elementary School
sights.description: Active school about 600m north of the hypocenter, preserving an A-bomb museum and shelter remains.

sights.name: Benex Dinosaur Museum
sights.description: Japan's third specialized dinosaur museum, opened in 2021, with a roughly 13 m T. rex replica seen only here.

sights.name: Nagasaki Atomic Bomb Museum
sights.description: Exhibits the August 9, 1945 bombing that killed about 150,000, events before it, Nagasaki's recovery, nuclear history, and peace.

sights.name: Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture
sights.description: Hands-on museum restoring the Nagasaki Magistrate's Office and showing 400 years of overseas exchange.

sights.name: Nagasaki Confucius Shrine and Historical Museum of China
sights.description: Confucius shrine built in 1893, with a museum of national-treasure-class Chinese artifacts.

sights.name: Gunkanjima Digital Museum
sights.description: Digital museum recreating Hashima coal mine, a 2015 World Heritage site, with 4K theater and VR closed-area views.

sights.name: Fukusai-ji Temple
sights.description: Large Obaku temple of the Four Fukuji, burned by the atomic bomb. Its 34m Kannon stands on a turtle-shaped mausoleum.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Takashi Nagai Memorial Hall
sights.description: Honors Dr. Takashi Nagai, who got leukemia from X-rays, was bombed 700m from the hypocenter, and kept calling for peace.

sights.name: Former Nagasaki British Consulate
sights.description: Two-story brick consulate rebuilt in 1908 to a design by British engineer William Cowan.

sights.name: Kagetsu
sights.description: Teahouse built in 1642 in Maruyama and designated a prefectural historic site in 1960.

sights.name: Siebold Memorial Museum
sights.description: Museum beside the Siebold house site honoring the German physician who came to Japan in 1823.

sights.name: Atomic-Bombed Camphor Tree
sights.description: Atomic-bombed camphor tree.

sights.name: Nagasaki Prefectural Art Museum
sights.description: Nature-harmonized museum designed by Kengo Kuma in Nagasaki Waterfront Forest Park. Collection features Nagasaki-related and Spanish art.

sights.name: Minamiyamate Traditional Buildings Preservation District
sights.description: Foreign settlement residential district on a hill overlooking Nagasaki Bay, with preserved Western-style houses.

sights.name: Manjusan Shofuku-ji Temple
sights.description: Obaku temple founded by Tetsushin Dohan. Main halls are national Important Cultural Properties. Its bell is Nagasaki's largest.

sights.name: Former Nagasaki Naigai Club (Dejima)
sights.description: 1903 British-style Meiji building of a club founded in 1899 for foreign and Japanese residents. Restaurant downstairs, settlement exhibits upstairs.

sights.name: Senshokaku (Not Open to the Public)
sights.description: Two-story wooden Western house built in 1904 by Sone Tatsuzo, still used as a guesthouse.

sights.name: Iojima Lighthouse
sights.description: Japan's first iron hexagonal Western-style lighthouse, first lit in 1871 and now unmanned.

sights.name: Gongenyama Observatory Park
sights.description: Summit park on about 198 m Gongenyama at Japan's southwesternmost point, with over 10,000 camellias.

sights.name: Mihara Garden
sights.description: Open garden by Chelsea Flower Show gold-medal designer Kazuyuki Ishihara, with Japanese and Western gardens in his hometown.

sights.name: Shitsu Village in Sotome
sights.description: Hidden Christians kept their faith themselves; Father de Rotz built Shitsu Church on a hill in 1882.

sights.name: Kinen Slope
sights.description: Famous slope overlooking Nagasaki Port and Oura Cathedral, used as a location for films and dramas.

sights.name: Higashiyamate Western-style Houses (7 Buildings)
sights.description: Seven similar wooden Western houses from the mid-1890s, six now a center, museum, and restaurant.

sights.name: Twenty-Six Martyrs Museum
sights.description: 1962 museum on Nishizaka marking 26 Christians executed in 1597, a Catholic pilgrimage site.

sights.name: Mini Dejima (inside Dejima)
sights.description: One-fifteenth Dejima model made in 1976 from Kawahara Keiga's painting, in the Dutch trading-post garden.

sights.name: Taki no Kannon
sights.description: Zen hall built in 1660, with a waterfall and a Kannon image donated from China.

sights.name: Higashiyamate No. 13 Building
sights.description: Mid-Meiji blue wooden house once home to French vice-consul Andre Boucry, with a heart-shaped hedge.

sights.name: Oura Observatory Park
sights.description: Hilltop park beside Oura Cathedral overlooking Higashiyamate and Nagasaki's night view.

sights.name: Shusaku Endo Literature Museum
sights.description: Museum in Sotome, setting of Endo's Silence, overlooking Sumonada and displaying manuscripts and belongings.

sights.name: Former Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Nagasaki Branch Memorial Hall
sights.description: Museum in the 1904 former bank, a national Important Cultural Property designed by Kikutaro Shimoda.

sights.name: Higashiyamate Traditional Buildings Preservation District
sights.description: Former foreign settlement on a hill overlooking Oura and the sea, preserving Western houses and Dutch Slope.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Science Museum (Starship)
sights.description: Opened in 1997; third-floor galleries renewed in 2018. Zones cover Nagasaki geology, local scientists, everyday technology, and virtual fireworks.

sights.name: Higashiyamate No. 12 Building (Former Foreign Settlement Private School History Museum)
sights.description: Oldest surviving Higashiyamate building, constructed in 1868 and a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Takashima Coal Mine Hokkei Pit Ruins
sights.description: Japan's first steam-powered Western shaft, 43m deep, by Glover and Saga Domain, worked until 1876.

sights.name: Dondon Slope
sights.description: Steep stone-paved slope in Minamiyamate, one of Nagasaki's 13 slope landscapes, overlooking the port.

sights.name: Megami Bridge
sights.description: Japan's sixth-longest cable-stayed bridge, linking Nagasaki's south and west, lit up at night.

sights.name: Naka no Chaya (Shimizu Kon Exhibition Hall)
sights.description: Mid-Edo teahouse of Maruyama brothel Chikugoya, also called Senzaiwa, sometimes used as a magistrate's rest stop.

sights.name: Wakamiya Inari Shrine
sights.description: Edo-period Inari shrine founded in 1673 at Irabayashi, also called Kinno Inari and visited by Ryoma.

sights.name: Daffodil Hill (Nagasaki Mozaki Dinosaur Park)
sights.description: Only site in Nagasaki Prefecture in the 100 Fragrance Landscapes, with about 10 million narcissus.

sights.name: Sotome Hidden Christian Culture Museum
sights.description: Museum beside Kurosaki Church displaying Maria Kannon, crosses, rosaries, prayers, and other Sotome Hidden Christian materials.

sights.name: Shitsu Cultural Village: Nagasaki City Sotome History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Museum of Sotome history, folklore, archaeology, industry, and religion, rich in Hidden Christian materials.

sights.name: Baien Migawari Tenmangu Shrine
sights.description: Tutelary shrine of Maruyama's pleasure quarter, founded in 1700 and cherished by courtesans.

sights.name: Ikeshima Coal Mine Ruins
sights.description: Kyushu's last coal mine, closed in 2001. Tunnels totaled about 90 km; former miners guide electric trolley rides.

sights.name: Nagasaki National Peace Memorial Hall for the Atomic Bomb Victims
sights.description: Place to mourn all atomic bomb victims and pray for peace, with name registers and testimonies.

sights.name: Heifuri Slope
sights.description: Famous Teramachi slopes to Kazagashira, where huge stones for Suwa Shrine's 1638 torii were lowered.

sights.name: Ryoma Street
sights.description: Slope used by Ryoma and Kameyama Shachu comrades, with memorial halls along the path.

sights.name: Sakamoto International Cemetery
sights.description: Newest of Nagasaki's three large international cemeteries, opened 1888 when Oura filled. Many foreign families who lived and died here.

sights.name: No. 3 Dry Dock (Not Open to the Public)
sights.description: Built 1901-1905, then the Orient's largest dock; original British motors and pumps remain in use.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Gunkanjima Museum
sights.description: Museum in Nomo overlooking Hashima, a World Heritage coal island, with panels and 4K video.

sights.name: Izumo Neighborhood Park
sights.description: Park on the 1926 Izumo water plant site, with views over Nagasaki Port.

sights.name: Nagasaki City History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Museum displaying archaeological finds, farm tools, local toys, and China, Portugal, and Netherlands materials.

sights.name: Noguchi Yataro Memorial Art Museum
sights.description: Museum of Nagasaki-linked Fauvist Noguchi Yataro, displaying about 20 of 340 works.

sights.name: Giant Cantilever Crane (Not Open to the Public)
sights.description: 1909 Scottish Appleby crane, Japan's first of its type, still used to ship turbines and propellers.

sights.name: Daitoku-ji Giant Camphor Tree
sights.description: A giant camphor with a 12.60 m trunk, among the prefecture's largest, estimated about 800 years old.

sights.name: Ono Village in Sotome
sights.description: Hidden Christians secretly enshrined their faith at a parish shrine; Ono Church was built nearby after the ban.

sights.name: Kosuge Ship Repair Dock Ruins
sights.description: Japan's first steam-powered Western slip dock. From November 2024 the hauling shed interior is guide-only on weekends and holidays.

sights.name: Nagasaki Prefectural Office
sights.description: Newly built in 2018, with an open entrance and eighth-floor terrace overlooking port and city.

sights.name: Nagasaki Peace Museum
sights.description: Museum founded with nationwide donations after Sada Masashi's appeal, showing conflict maps, peace literature, and children's photos.

sights.name: Daitoku-ji Park
sights.description: Green park where Daitoku-ji stood until 1868, home to an estimated 800-year-old camphor, a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Great Camphor Tree of Kanzen-ji
sights.description: Camphor tree at Kanzen-ji, 20 meters tall with an 8-meter trunk girth.

sights.name: Former Wooden Pattern Shop (Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagasaki Shipyard Museum)
sights.description: Closed for construction since April 2020. The 1898 red-brick shop is the shipyard's oldest factory and a World Heritage component.

sights.name: Onakao Rice Terraces
sights.description: About 450 paddies on 8 hectares along the Konoura River, one of Japan's 100 rice terraces.

sights.name: Dojindo, Kannondo and Tenkodo in the Former Tojin Yashiki
sights.description: Halls of the 1689 Chinese quarter, dated about 1691, 1736 and 1737, were later destroyed by fire.

sights.name: Shinden-an Hermitage
sights.description: Villa built by Ga Choshin in Katafuchi; facility rental resumed in June 2026.

sights.name: Takashima Shuhan Former Residence
sights.description: Villa of late-Edo gunnery expert Takashima Shuhan, also called Reishoken and Useiro.

sights.name: Prayer Hill Picture Book Museum
sights.description: Picture book museum in a Nagasaki Western-style building near Oura Cathedral and Glover Garden.

sights.name: Kiyomizu-dera
sights.description: Founded in 1623; its 1668 main hall blends Japanese and Chinese Obaku styles.

sights.name: Inasa Goshin-ji International Cemetery
sights.description: Rare international cemetery at Jodo-sect Goshin-ji below night-famous Mount Inasa. Many nations and faiths, mostly sea or city deaths.

sights.name: Siebold Residence Site
sights.description: National historic site of Siebold's Narutaki home and school, where he taught medicine after coming to Dejima.

sights.name: Maruyama Oranda-zaka
sights.description: Stone-step slope from Sofuku-ji to the tram street, once used by Dutch residents.

sights.name: Nagasaki Kenban
sights.description: Maruyama office managing geisha practice and bookings, in a wooden former pleasure house over 100 years old.

sights.name: Shitsu Cultural Village: Silence Monument
sights.description: Monument built by a friend of author Shusaku Endo, overlooking the sea and the Shusaku Endo Literary Museum.

sights.name: Daion-ji
sights.description: One of Nagasaki's three great temples, with an over 300-year-old ginkgo and a magistrate's grave.

sights.name: Shitsu Cultural Village: Former Shitsu Aid Center
sights.description: Workshop built by Father de Rotz in 1883 for women's independence, with weaving and food processing.

sights.name: Statue of Sakamoto Ryoma
sights.description: Bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma on Mount Kazagashira, made in 1989 by Yamazaki Kazukuni.

sights.name: Minamiyamate Rest House (Former Shimizu Residence)
sights.description: Bakumatsu stone residence beside Glover Garden, open as a rest house since 2003.

sights.name: Shitsu Cultural Village: Father de Rotz Memorial Hall
sights.description: 1885 sardine-net factory designed by French priest Marc Marie de Rotz, opened as a memorial hall.

sights.name: Hidden Christian Gravestone
sights.description: Hidden Christian gravestone without a posthumous name, investigated three times but still standing.

sights.name: Enpuku-ji
sights.description: Kukai practice site atop 400 steps, with incense traces in a rock hollow, called western Koyasan.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Hall
sights.description: City hall opened January 2023, with a free 19th-floor observatory at 80 meters, open until 9:30pm.

sights.name: Nakashima River Stone Bridges
sights.description: Stone bridges built across Nakashima River from 1634; several restored after the 1982 flood.

sights.name: Takashima Coal Museum
sights.description: Since 1988, preserves Takashima coal-mine items such as man-cars and a Hashima model in front.

sights.name: Kogakura International Submarine Cable Landing Station
sights.description: Restored landing house for cables laid in 1871 to Shanghai and Vladivostok, starting Japan's international communications.

sights.name: Nagasaki Minamiyamate Townscape Preservation Center
sights.description: Quality house built by Briton Wilson Walker in mid-Meiji. Shows a 1/500 settlement model and old townscape photos.

sights.name: Kawaharaoike Park
sights.description: Largest natural freshwater lake in the prefecture, with designated woods, a beach, and camping.

sights.name: Kabashima Lighthouse Park
sights.description: 1932 white circular lighthouse with Amakusa and Goto views, birds, and about 100 cherries.

sights.name: Nagasaki City Minamiyamate Rest House
sights.description: Edo-period foreign settlement house near Glover Garden, with free viewing and old photo displays.

sights.name: Mikaeri Yanagi
sights.description: A willow planted in the Meiji era near the former pleasure-quarter gate, where visitors looked back.

sights.name: Oga Family Gi Shien Brothers' Grave
sights.description: Chinese-style tomb enshrining Oga founder Gi Shien and his elder brother.

sights.name: Shokunin-zukushi Carvings
sights.description: Thirty colored panels of medieval craftsmen at Matsumori Tenmangu, dedicated in 1713.

sights.name: Nagasaki Higashiyamate Townscape Preservation Center
sights.description: One of seven Western houses designated a city tangible cultural property in 1989. Photo panels on floor one.

sights.name: Stone Bridge in Honkawachi Upper Reservoir
sights.description: Likely late-Edo stone arch bridge, submerged since 1889 and visible only in drought.

sights.name: Nagasaki Venus Observation Monument and Platform
sights.description: Monument to French astronomer Janssen's successful 1874 Venus transit observation; platform found 24 m east in 1993.

sights.name: Kurosaki Nagata Wetland Nature Park
sights.description: Eco-park of about 9.8 hectares on former rice fields, opened in 2003 along Route 202.

sights.name: Omoikiri Bridge Site
sights.description: Stone monument near Shianbashi, where men resolved to enter the pleasure quarter.

sights.name: Nagasaki Park
sights.description: Nagasaki's oldest park by Suwa Shrine, with monuments, Japan's oldest decorative fountain, and an animal area.

sights.name: Ogawa Kite Shop Nagasaki Kite Museum
sights.description: Shop museum displaying traditional Nagasaki kite-making tools and a handmade workshop.

sights.name: Giant Mottled Eel Habitat
sights.description: Kabashima well, the northern habitat of giant mottled eels, designated a national natural monument in 1923.

sights.name: Former Honda Family Residence
sights.description: Considered the prefecture's oldest farmhouse, estimated around the Meiwa era (1764-72).

sights.name: Hodakayama Beacon Ruins
sights.description: Beacon ordered in 1638 after the Shimabara Rebellion, alerting the port until 1868.

sights.name: Iojima Bridge
sights.description: 876-meter bridge opened in March 2011, linking Koyagi and formerly boat-only Iojima.

sights.name: Furukawa-machi Tenmangu Torii
sights.description: Hizen-style stone torii dated 1641 that survived the city fire of 1663.

sights.name: Kogakura Folded Strata
sights.description: Rare recumbent fold, mainly slab sandstone, exposed in 1962 on the cliff north of Kogakura housing area.

sights.name: Nagasaki Battery Site: Uomidake Battery Ruins
sights.description: Uomidake retains well-preserved battery remains and powder-magazine stone warehouses from Nagasaki Port defenses.

sights.name: Nomozaki Small Aquarium Coral Reef House
sights.description: Small aquarium in a former Nomozaki factory, displaying coral reefs and local fish in about 25 tanks.

sights.name: Pintoko Slope
sights.description: Steep slope from the Kogoshima cemetery to Nagasaki Prefectural Minami High School's main gate.

sights.name: Winter Cherry at Nishiyama Shrine
sights.description: Winter cherry planted in 1897 at Nishiyama Shrine, blooming from mid-December to early February.

sights.name: Hayashi and Kanbai Family Cemetery
sights.description: Side-by-side graves of the Hayashi and Kanbai families, descended from famed interpreter Hayashi Doei.

sights.name: Wakimisaki Morning Glory Community
sights.description: Designated morning glory community from 50 m Gion Mountain to the shore, with blue-purple flowers.

sights.name: Tanase Beachrock
sights.description: Beachrock formed about 6,000 years ago, exposed at low tide, and a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Tokai Family Graves
sights.description: Chinese-style cemetery of the Tokai interpreter family, completed in 1677 with 29 tombstones.

sights.name: Kannon-ji
sights.description: Said to be founded by Gyoki in 709, with a nationally designated Kannon statue.

sights.name: Susukizuka Haiku Monument
sights.description: Haiku monument to Mukai Kyorai (1651-1704), born in Nagasaki, a Basho disciple who spread Basho-style haikai there.

sights.name: Utsutsugawa Ware Kiln Site
sights.description: Kiln that produced Utsutsugawa brush-mark pottery for about 60 years from 1691.

sights.name: Great Camphor Tree of Kamado Shrine
sights.description: Camphor near Kamado Shrine, about 25 meters tall and said to be over 350 years old.

sights.name: Ichinose-guchi
sights.description: Old Nagasaki Kaido entrance at the 1653 Ichinose Bridge, now the Hotarujaya tram terminal.

sights.name: Mogi Plant Fossil Bed
sights.description: Mudstone at Shirahama Beach with 52 plant fossil species, thought about 10 million years old.

sights.name: Oura International Cemetery
sights.description: Cemetery opened in 1861 beside the foreign settlement; most burials are American sailors.

sights.name: Yuhigaoka Observatory
sights.description: Overlooks Goto-nada near Iojima Lighthouse; binoculars show Takashima and Gunkanjima, with fine sunsets.

sights.name: Iojima Lighthouse Memorial Hall (Former Lighthouse Staff Quarters)
sights.description: Western-style former lighthouse staff house, a prefectural tangible cultural property, opened as a hall in 1988.

sights.name: Nameshi Daijingu Sacred Grove
sights.description: Sacred grove around Nameshi Daijingu, founded in 1668, covering a low hill with large trees.

sights.name: Gongenyama Park Observatory
sights.description: Quiet park at Takashima's highest point, overlooking Hashima, the Goto Islands, and sunsets.

sights.name: Furubashi (Nakagawa Bridge)
sights.description: 1654 stone bridge over the Narutaki River, the smallest on this water system at 5.1 meters.

sights.name: Kotai-ji Temple Bell
sights.description: Temple bell recast in 1702, the only Nagasaki bell cast by a Saga foundryman.

sights.name: Mukai Family Cemetery at Kodai-ji Temple
sights.description: Cemetery at Kodai-ji with four gravestones of the Mukai family, hereditary book inspectors.

sights.name: Toishi Six Jizo Pagoda
sights.description: Saga-type six-Jizo stone pagoda dated 1604, with high-relief figures on lotus pedestals.

sights.name: Miyazuri Yaman-kami Sacred Grove
sights.description: Small sacred grove of over 30 species, including unusually large mokkoku trees.

sights.name: Kozakihana Park
sights.description: Mainland Japan's westernmost point, with a monument, lawn, blue sea, and tide pools.

sights.name: Kujukushima
sights.description: 208 islands stretching 25 km north from Sasebo Port to Hirado Strait, called Japan's densest.

sights.name: Hario Radio Towers
sights.description: Three concrete radio towers about 136 meters tall, completed by the Imperial Navy in 1922.

sights.name: Tenkaiho Observatory
sights.description: Observatory at 165 meters offering a 180-degree panorama of Kujukushima and Sasebo Port.

sights.name: Saikai Bridge and New Saikai Bridge
sights.description: 1955 arch bridge spanning 316m, 43m above Hario Seto rapids, beside a glass-windowed new bridge.

sights.name: JMSDF Sasebo Historical Museum (Sail Tower)
sights.description: Museum explaining Imperial Navy and Maritime Self-Defense Force history, with models and an observation lobby.

sights.name: Jufuku-ji
sights.description: Offers limited inverted autumn-maple and early-summer greenery views reflected in the hall.

sights.name: Ishidake Observatory
sights.description: Observatory on 191-meter Ishidake, about 15 minutes from Kujukushima Zoo, with 360-degree views.

sights.name: Mukyudo Cave
sights.description: Huge air-raid shelter dug in 1943 by school teachers and pupils for 500 children.

sights.name: Yumihari-dake Observatory
sights.description: Panoramic observatory of Sasebo, Kujukushima and Goto-nada, listed in Japan's 100 night views.

sights.name: Ohashi Kannon Stone Bridge
sights.description: One of Hirado's eight views: a natural stone bridge like a floating bridge beyond an elegant garden.

sights.name: Former Sasebo Naval District Air Defense Command Post Ruins
sights.description: Two-level underground air-defense command post of 1,900 square meters, completed in 1942 under the naval district office.

sights.name: Former Sasebo Naval District Triumphal Memorial Hall (Sasebo Civic Cultural Hall)
sights.description: Donated and built in 1923; returned from US use in 1977 and a civic cultural hall since 1982.

sights.name: Awashima Shrine
sights.description: Shrine on a Kujukushima island enshrining three deities who protect women, fertility, and women's illnesses.

sights.name: Sasebo Port
sights.description: Long a naval and commercial port, now partly used by the US Navy and Maritime Self-Defense Force.

sights.name: Mikawachi Sarayama
sights.description: Pottery district started with kilns in Mikawachi, Eie, and Kihara, where many kilns keep the tradition.

sights.name: Fukui Cave
sights.description: Site with cultural layers of the Paleolithic-to-Jomon transition and tools over 30,000 years old.

sights.name: Senryugataki Falls Park
sights.description: Seventh of Hirado's eight views: about 20-meter men's and women's falls.

sights.name: Megane-iwa
sights.description: Rock 10 meters high and 20 wide, naturally pierced like spectacles, one of Hirado's eight views.

sights.name: Fujiyama Shrine
sights.description: Kyushu's leading wisteria site, with prefectural natural monuments and an 800-year-old sacred tree.

sights.name: Funakoshi Observatory
sights.description: Lowest Kujukushima Eight Views lookout, so islands feel close. Ink-painting beauty in rain. Step-free for wheelchairs.

sights.name: Utsuwa History Museum
sights.description: Museum of Sasebo pottery from Jomon to Mikawachi ware, with a world-oldest-class bean-pattern replica.

sights.name: Sasebo Flower Garden
sights.description: Year-round flower garden of about 12,000 tsubo with peonies, koi, and mandarin ducks.

sights.name: Haiki Shrine
sights.description: Shrine reached by over 100 steps, overlooking Haiki town and sunsets, and popular for first sunrise.

sights.name: Senpuku-ji Cave
sights.description: Cave discovered by local junior-high students, source of pottery about 16,000 years old.

sights.name: Mikawachi Ware Traditional Industry Hall (Mikawachi Ware Museum)
sights.description: Closed for major repairs from March 31, 2026 until planned autumn 2028; shows Edo-Meiji white porcelain.

sights.name: Fukui Cave Museum
sights.description: Museum of Fukui Cave, a Paleolithic-to-Jomon site, displaying Important Cultural Property finds and a life-size diorama.

sights.name: Hana no Mori Park
sights.description: Vast park with about 40,000 seasonal flowers and trees, and a hidden cherry blossom site.

sights.name: Nogata Coast (Tsushimase Lighthouse)
sights.description: Cliff-lined rias coast with grasslands on northern Uku and symbolic Tsushimase Lighthouse.

sights.name: Sasebo Heavy Industries (SSK)
sights.description: Historic shipyard, locally called SSK, that built the 1962 tanker Nissho Maru; 1913 crane still works.

sights.name: Sasebo Higashiyama Naval Cemetery (Higashi Park)
sights.description: Cemetery for over 170,000 navy dead, with 62 joint and 437 individual monuments.

sights.name: Red Buckwheat Village
sights.description: Local farmers grow red-flowering Takane Ruby buckwheat; flower viewing is usually late October to early November.

sights.name: Dainen-ji Bell Tower Gate
sights.description: City-designated Jodo temple founded in 1541; its Edo bell-tower gate survived a 1991 fire.

sights.name: Uragashira Repatriation Memorial Peace Park and Museum
sights.description: Peace park and museum where about 1.4 million repatriates landed between 1945 and 1950.

sights.name: Fukuseki Kannon Seigan-ji
sights.description: Temple enshrining an Eleven-faced Kannon said to be carved by Gyoki in 710, one of seven in Kyushu.

sights.name: Udokoshi Observatory
sights.description: Historic Yumiharidake lookout known since the Taisho era. Views Kujukushima and Pearl Sea Resort. Spring azaleas.

sights.name: Uku Island Jogatake Observatory
sights.description: Summit about 259 m overlooks the Goto Islands. Wartime radar remains were designated Japan Heritage in 2017.

sights.name: Iwashita Cave
sights.description: Cave at 200 m on Mount Ishimori where over 20 Jomon burials were excavated.

sights.name: Pothole Park
sights.description: 500-meter riverside park opened in 1991 along the Saza River, named for its countless potholes.

sights.name: Uku Island Yaku Shrine
sights.description: Relocated in the Kamakura period with a spirit from Otokoyama Hachimangu to quell an epidemic.

sights.name: Former Sasebo Naval Barracks Ruins
sights.description: Facilities in Sasebo Park of a corps that trained over a million youths for 56 years until the war's end.

sights.name: Mount Atago
sights.description: Fuji-shaped 259-meter mountain in northern Sasebo, called Ainoura Fuji, with a February festival and wish stone.

sights.name: Iimori Shrine
sights.description: Ainoura local shrine with a large catfish statue, a healing legend, and white catfish fortunes.

sights.name: Miyajidake Shrine
sights.description: Shrine famous for warding off misfortune, with a covered approach and vermilion halls reachable by car.

sights.name: Kuroshima Village
sights.description: Migrant Hidden Christians continued organized faith tacitly tolerated by Buddhist temples, then built a central church.

sights.name: Former Residence of Kusumoto Tanzan
sights.description: House built in 1832 by the father of Confucian scholar Kusumoto Tanzan, with a Confucian shrine.

sights.name: Marudeyama Observation Post Ruins
sights.description: Sasebo Fortress observation post built from 1897 to protect the naval port. No shots fired in the Russo-Japanese War.

sights.name: Uku Island Koshima Shrine
sights.description: Taira district tutelary shrine built by Taira no Iemori; festivals carry a roughly 400 kg portable shrine.

sights.name: Kameyama Hachimangu
sights.description: Sasebo's representative shrine, one of the Nagasaki Three Shrines, and naval-port guardian since the Meiji era.

sights.name: Sasebo City Museum Shimase Art Center
sights.description: Beside Shimase Park, it shows 12,000-year-old pottery, a cave model, and art and citizen exhibitions.

sights.name: Uku Island Hamakata Fureai Hall
sights.description: The island's only hands-on facility on ama diver history, whaling culture, and the old Miyazaki Cannery.

sights.name: Sechibaru Coal Mine Museum (Former Matsuura Coal Mine Office)
sights.description: Opened in 1975 in the former Matsuura Coal Mine Office; Western-style stone exterior is a prefectural tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Toko-ji (Uku Island)
sights.description: Holds mausoleums of seven Goto domain founder generations, beginning with Uku Iemori.

sights.name: Fuzan Shrine
sights.description: Tenmangu subsidiary shrine to Korai Baba, a Mikawachi teacher buried here after dying at 100 in 1670.

sights.name: Giant Cycad of Miura Shrine (Uku Island)
sights.description: Prefectural natural-monument cycad at Miura Shrine, raised as a girl's incarnation.

sights.name: Former Sasebo Fortress Kokubi Battery Ruins
sights.description: Sasebo Fortress battery built in 1900; it never saw combat, and its guns were removed by 1942.

sights.name: Emukae Honjin and Yamashita Family Motogura
sights.description: Prefectural historic site where Hirado lords stayed, with a water-harp cave and nail-free storehouse.

sights.name: Hoshitsukushi Park
sights.description: Park about five minutes by car from Sasebo Station, overlooking the port and famous for cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Shiradake Shrine
sights.description: Founded circa 1578 by Goto Koreaki. September festival offers Hirado Kagura, a national intangible folk property.

sights.name: Uku Island Taira no Iemori Landing Site (Funagakushi)
sights.description: Inlet where storm-stranded Taira no Iemori hid his boat; Hitakizaki cape is a sunset spot.

sights.name: Takashima Bandake Observatory
sights.description: A Kujukushima Eight Views lookout toward Hirado and the Goto Islands, the only one for sunrise.

sights.name: Tenjin Park
sights.description: Park overlooking Sasebo Port with cherries, azaleas, and irises; closed for road work until March 2030.

sights.name: Saiko-ji
sights.description: Temple with a rare 260-year-old double-blooming Omurazakura, a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Uku Island Historical Museum
sights.description: Displays excavated artifacts and folk cultural properties, including Paleolithic microblades and Yayoi coffins.

sights.name: Sechibaru-Yoshii Stone Bridge Group
sights.description: Seventeen stone bridges built mainly from late Meiji through early Showa by Hirado stonemasons for coal transport.

sights.name: Toso Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Nyoen, who perfected Mikawachi white porcelain and founded the domain workshop at age 34.

sights.name: Nishikyushu Warehouse Maehata No. 1 and Hizukushi Warehouse Group
sights.description: Nine former naval supply warehouses built from the Taisho era into the early 1940s remain in Hizukushi.

sights.name: Takagozaki Ship Guardhouse Ruins
sights.description: Remains of a Hirado Domain ship guardhouse that policed foreign ships under the Nagasaki Magistrate. Old stone jetty remains.

sights.name: Kuroshima Kushinohama Dike
sights.description: Nagasaki Prefecture's largest dike, over 300 m, formed about 8 million years ago and visible at low tide.

sights.name: Mikawachi Ware
sights.description: White porcelain with delicate blue gosu painting, including karako designs and openwork taking half a year.

sights.name: Kuroshima Site of Faith Revival, Deguchi House
sights.description: The island's first Mass was held here in 1872 after hidden Christians returned to Catholicism.

sights.name: Naotani Castle Ruins
sights.description: Mountain castle likely built by the Shisa clan in the mid-13th century, on a 50-meter cliff by the Fukui River.

sights.name: Tonbai Walls and Carriage Road
sights.description: Kiln-brick walls colored by ash, beside a carriage road ridged so horses do not slip uphill.

sights.name: Kuroshima Neya Giant Sasanqua
sights.description: One of northern Nagasaki's largest sasanquas, about 250 years old; a Sasebo City natural monument.

sights.name: Mikawachi East and West Kiln Sites
sights.description: East kiln 120 meters, used until 1937; west kiln 100 meters, used until 1941; both were domain kilns.

sights.name: Koyasu Kannon Great Camphor
sights.description: Camphor 23 m tall and about 500 years old, a prefectural natural monument since 1970.

sights.name: Kuroshima Warabe Observatory
sights.description: Observatory overlooking the Nagasakibana and Kakisebana cliffs, with Sakito and Kamigoto visible on clear days.

sights.name: Uku Island Horikawa Ebisu Shrine (Whale Ebisu)
sights.description: Edo-period worship hall of Koshiki Shrine, praying for large whaling catches and safe voyages.

sights.description: 1496 castle ruins, a natural fortress surrounded on three sides by the Ariake Sea.

sights.name: Town Where Carp Swim
sights.description: Shinmachi streams where residents released colored carp into abundant spring water, a highlight of watery Shimabara.

sights.name: Debris Flow Damaged House Preservation Park
sights.description: Park preserving nine houses damaged by the August 1992 debris flow to show disaster-prevention importance.

sights.name: Shimeiso Spring Garden
sights.description: Late Meiji villa garden with four-direction views, a spring-fed carp pond, pines, and maples.

sights.name: Shimabara Castle
sights.description: Built from 1618 over seven years by Matsukura Shigemasa; also called Moritake Castle.

sights.name: Heisei Shinzan
sights.description: Unzen lava dome named in 1996 to commemorate the long disaster and new recovery.

sights.name: Ayugaeri Falls
sights.description: Waterfall about 14 meters high where sweetfish once returned, with rock play and flowing somen.

sights.name: Ariake Forest Flower Park
sights.description: 35,000-square-meter flower park at Mount Mai's foot, with seasonal blooms and views of Ariake Sea, Aso, and Unzen.

sights.name: Former Onokoba Elementary School Damaged Building and Sabo Future Hall
sights.description: School burned by the September 1991 pyroclastic flow, preserved beside a hall of disaster exhibits.

sights.name: Mount Unzen Disaster Memorial Hall Gamadasu Dome
sights.description: Museum of the Unzen eruption from November 1990 for about five years; renewed March 1, 2025.

sights.name: Shimabara Hibariyama Flower Park
sights.description: Flower park overlooking Heisei Shinzan, with spring flowers, 10 million cosmos, and 60,000 sunflowers.

sights.name: Omisaki Station
sights.description: Japan's closest station to the sea, an unmanned Shimabara Railway stop with the Ariake Sea directly behind it.

sights.name: Samurai Residences
sights.description: Preserved Shimo-no-cho samurai street, 406.8 meters long and 5.6 meters wide, west of Shimabara Castle.

sights.name: Sezumezaki Lighthouse
sights.description: Southern-tip lighthouse on Shimabara Peninsula; Hayasaki Seto whirlpools reach 20 m across at March-June spring tides.

sights.name: Hara Castle Holy Maria Kannon Hall
sights.description: Ten-meter wooden statue, the world's largest Maria image, carved over 40 years to mourn Shimabara-Amakusa Rebellion victims.

sights.name: Shimabara Mayuyama Road
sights.description: Eight-kilometer road around Mayuyama near Heisei Shinzan, Japan's newest mountain, for volcanic sightseeing.

sights.name: Arima Christian Heritage Museum
sights.description: Introduces Hara Castle Ruins, Hinoe Castle Ruins, and Arima Seminary in Nagasaki Christian history.

sights.name: Minamishimabara Sunflower Fields
sights.description: Sunflower fields in Minamishimabara, planted by locals after harvest, not run as a tourist farm.

sights.name: Futagoiwa Rock
sights.description: Head-shaped rock carved by waves from ancient volcanic debris-flow deposits; one of two remains.

sights.name: Harayama Dolmen Group
sights.description: Japan's oldest and largest dolmen group, from about the 4th century BC, with over 100 tombs.

sights.name: Hinoe Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins of Christian lord Arima Harunobu, who founded Japan's first European secondary school.

sights.name: Kuchinotsu History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Museum richly displaying materials on Kuchinotsu's past and present as a historic natural harbor.

sights.name: Nanban Ship Arrival Site
sights.description: Nagasaki-designated historic site of 1567 Portuguese ship arrivals and a 1579 Christian mission base.

sights.name: Tatsuishi Coast
sights.description: Coast showing Unzen's earliest layers from 500,000 years ago, above former seafloor deposits and debris-flow layers.

sights.name: Fukae Suwa Shrine Grove
sights.description: Grove of Suwa Shrine enshrined in 1428, with seven large camphor trees, the largest 6.6 meters around.

sights.name: Shimabara City Ariake General Cultural Hall (Green Wave)
sights.description: Complex with a 700-seat hall and galleries; its museum shows Jomon remains, and the library holds over 70,000 books.

sights.name: Hamanokawa Spring
sights.description: Spring with four washing sections used in order by purpose; the traditional custom is still kept.

sights.name: Blue Barbershop
sights.description: Blue wooden barbershop built in 1923, Western in front and Japanese in back, now a rest spot.

sights.name: Seibo Park (Seibo Memorial Hall)
sights.description: Park honoring Peace Statue sculptor Kitamura Seibo, with about 60 works and views of Hara Castle Ruins.

sights.name: Arie Tawaraishi Observatory
sights.description: Overlooks Arie from Route 57 between Unzen and Shimabara, with Shiranui Sea, Ariake Sea, and clear-day Mt. Aso views.

sights.name: Reikyu Park
sights.description: City-center park with about 250 Somei-Yoshino cherries and about 3,000 Hirado azaleas.

sights.name: Hayauo River and Inohara Hardware Store
sights.description: Heisei-era stream from Tsuki well spring water, with fish and wasabi. Bacteria-free, 15 degrees, 150 liters per minute.

sights.name: Tonosumi Falls
sights.description: Falls in upper Shimizu River's Tonosumi Gorge, loved for summer coolness and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Hakariishi Spring Water Spot
sights.description: A concave channel-bed stone splits spring water north and south. Shimabara City tangible folk cultural property.

sights.name: Hanabusa Observatory
sights.description: Panoramic viewpoint over islands, mountains, and Hayasaki Peninsula, with visible ancient volcanic strata.

sights.name: Shimabara Castle Moat Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: 250 Somei-Yoshino cherries bloom along 1.3 kilometers of the castle moat, with red night lanterns.

sights.name: Sunset Hill
sights.description: Scenic spot in Eco Park Ronshobaru, Kita-Arima, with fine views of sunsets over Tachibana Bay.

sights.name: Mayuyama Erosion Control Memorial Park
sights.description: Memorial park at Mayuyama's foot with Seibo Kitamura's Kanzeon statue, cherry trees, and sports fields.

sights.name: Fukae Buried Cultural Properties and Eruption Disaster Museum
sights.description: Displays excavated pottery and other artifacts, plus photos of the Unzen Fugendake eruption disaster.

sights.name: Iwatoyama Grove
sights.description: 97-meter mountain; rare plants designated a national natural monument in 1928. Also a Kannon faith site.

sights.name: Senbongi Observatory
sights.description: Overlook where pyroclastic flows and heat blasts devastated the district on June 23-24, 1993.

sights.name: Gonda Park
sights.description: Hilltop park at 100-140m with views, spring cherries and azaleas, autumn cosmos, and sunsets.

sights.name: Spectacles Bridge (Minamishimabara City)
sights.description: Stone arch bridge built in 1853, called the oldest public stone bridge on the Shimabara Peninsula.

sights.name: Amagase Kofun
sights.description: Late Kofun-period corridor-style stone chamber tomb with front and rear rooms, stones now exposed.

sights.name: Shinwa Spring
sights.description: City-center spring across from Yutorogi footbath; people drink the water or take it home.

sights.name: Hayasaki Basalt
sights.description: One of Shimabara Peninsula's oldest rocks, erupted about 4.3 million years ago, with Hawaii-like black lava.

activities.description: Relax while viewing the deep-blue sea horizon; next to Miuda Beach and enjoyable for the whole family.

activities.name: Komoda Beach

activities.name: Komodahama Shrine Grand Festival

activities.description: Hilltop panorama of sky and sea. Tsushima fishing fires sparkle at night. Free foot bath from April to November.

activities.name: Mitsushima Town Beach

activities.name: Shinwa no Sato Nature Park
activities.description: Nature park midway up Mt. Eboshi, with camping, a Japanese garden, and guided sea kayaking.

activities.name: Meboro Dam Equestrian Park
activities.description: Park in northern Tsushima where native Taishu horses can be viewed, fed, and ridden.

activities.name: Aoshio no Sato (Oura Campground and Beach)
activities.description: Nature-rich Oura campsite and beach with six-person bungalows, rental tents, and summer swimming.

sights.name: Bansho-in Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1615 as the So family temple. Main hall rebuilt 1879; Tsushima's oldest gate and 132 steps remain.

sights.name: Kaneda Castle
sights.description: Ancient mountain castle built in 667 on Tsushima to prepare for Tang and Silla invasion.

sights.name: Tsushima Museum
sights.description: Museum opened April 30, 2022, presenting Tsushima history, art, folklore, nature, and So family documents.

sights.name: Himekamiyama Battery Ruins
sights.description: Meiji battery of red brick and sandstone, finished in 1901 and later fitted with six 28cm howitzers.

sights.name: Ayumodoshi Nature Park
sights.description: Special protection area where granite-covered Segawa River forms a rare landscape, busy in summer.

sights.name: Tsushima Wildlife Conservation Center
sights.description: Base protecting Tsushima's rare wildlife, explaining the leopard cat, viewable through a one-way mirror.

sights.name: Kaneishi Castle Ruins
sights.description: Ruins expanded in 1665 with no castle keep; walls, a gate site, and a garden pond remain.

sights.name: Hatchokaku
sights.description: Mossy stone tower in ancient forest, a once-forbidden Tendo ritual site now planted with cherry and azalea.

sights.name: Tsushima Domain Ofunae Ruins
sights.description: Inlet built in 1663 at the Kuta River mouth, with four jetties and five docks; original stone embankments remain.

sights.name: Shushi Maple Avenue
sights.description: Maples line about 7 km along the Shushi River, a walking course known for Tsushima's finest autumn colors.

sights.name: Shimizuyama Castle Ruins
sights.description: Built in 1591 for Hideyoshi's Korea campaign, with three baileys and well-preserved gate courts. Nationally designated monument.

sights.name: Amatsukami Takuzutama Shrine
sights.description: Shrine famous for a sacred-rock altar without a building, listed in 870 at Tendo Mountain's foot.

sights.name: Former Nisshinkan Gate (with Stone Wall)
sights.description: Prefectural cultural property; So clan gate of late-Edo rank, later used by Nisshinkan domain school.

sights.name: Entsu-ji Temple
sights.description: Temple behind which So family graves stand, with a 13th-century bronze Yakushi and early Joseon bell.

sights.name: Yutaka Battery Ruins
sights.description: Mounted Akagi's scrapped main gun, then the world's largest, never fired; access is fully closed for now.

sights.name: Ikoku no Mieru Oka Observatory
sights.description: Observation tower about 50 km from Busan, viewing fishing lights and the Busan cityscape.

sights.name: Manzeki Observatory
sights.description: Overlooks the army-dug Manzeki channel, Manzeki Bridge, and whirlpools between Aso and Miura bays.

sights.name: Great Ginkgo of Kin
sights.description: Said to be a 1,500-year-old ginkgo at Chosho-ji, Japan's oldest, 12.5 m around and 40 m tall.

sights.name: Stone-Roofed Warehouses
sights.description: Shiine storehouses roofed with thick sandstone slabs, set apart from houses to survive fires.

sights.name: Monument to the Shipwrecked Joseon Interpreters
sights.description: In 1703, 108 Joseon interpreters died in a shipwreck near Wanoura; the 1991 monument base uses 112 spirit stones.

sights.name: Kizaka Gozenhama Park
sights.description: Coastal site where the Yakuma festival stacks stones to pray for boys' growth and harvests.

sights.name: Saozaki Park
sights.description: 49.5 km from Busan, offering mountain and night views, wartime batteries, gardens, and Japan's northwest tip monument.

sights.name: Japan Sea Naval Battle Monument (Tonozaki Park)
sights.description: 1905 monument to the Japan Sea naval battle; local people aided 143 Russian sailors who landed here.

sights.name: Toyotama Wild Boar Wall
sights.description: Well-preserved stone walls near Shirako Beach, long called boar walls from Genroku-Hoei hunts, though that is doubted.

sights.name: Tatsurayama Primeval Forest
sights.description: National natural monument: unlogged laurel forest below 559-meter Tatsurayama, trees averaging 200 years.

sights.name: Waniura Park
sights.description: Largest wild grove of Chinese fringe trees in Japan, a national natural monument also called Umiterashi.

sights.name: Seizan-ji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 858 after a temple fire; renamed in 1511, changed from Shingon to Rinzai, and offers lodging.

sights.name: Aoumi Village
sights.description: Valley village of cliffs over 30 meters and terraced fields, keeping a dual-grave custom until modern times.

sights.name: Ajiro Ripple Marks and Laundry Rock
sights.description: Among Japan's largest tongue-shaped ripple marks, formed by currents on Taishu Group sandstone.

sights.name: Mutsugozen Shrine Great Ginkgo
sights.description: A vigorous Tsushima ginkgo about 21 meters tall, with a trunk over 6 meters, second to Koto's great tree.

sights.name: Asahiyama Kofun
sights.description: Stone-chamber tombs behind Hekireki Shrine yielded a Han-style mirror, magatama, iron weapons, and Sue ware in 1948.

sights.name: Sweet Potato Elder Harada Saburoemon Monument
sights.description: Honors Harada Saburoemon, said to have brought banned seed potatoes from Satsuma and spread them across Tsushima.

sights.name: Joseon Tongsinsa Monument
sights.description: Twelve Joseon missions visited Japan from 1607 to 1811, parties of about 500 bringing learning and arts.

sights.name: Narutaki Falls
sights.description: Tsushima's tallest falls, 15 meters, named for echoing through the mountains, a dragon-god site.

sights.name: Tonokubi Site
sights.description: National historic site: five late-Yayoi stone coffins with bronze spears, a TLV mirror, beads, and Korean pottery.

sights.name: Fishing Fires
sights.description: A Tsushima seasonal scene: many fishing-boat lights color the night sea like a city on the water.

sights.name: Bunka no Sato Local Museum
sights.description: Hilltop local museum in Nii displaying Jomon and Yayoi finds plus modern farm and fishing tools.

sights.name: Shimo Shiratake Primeval Forest
sights.description: Japan's foremost site where Japanese and Korean plants coexist, on 519-meter Shiratake.

sights.name: Tsunashima
sights.description: Three Kotsunaura islands famed for sunsets and designated in Nagasaki's New 100 selections.

sights.name: Sajihara-kan Koraimon (Former Sajihara Castle Gate)
sights.description: Third gate of the 1678 lord's residence, toppled by a 1987 typhoon and restored in 1989.

sights.name: Chiromo Ripple Marks
sights.description: Ripple marks in Taishu Group sandstone, exposed by a cliff collapse during a 1952 typhoon.

sights.name: Imayashiki Fire Walls
sights.description: Fire walls built after 1841 in Fuchu to prevent fire spread; a rare prefectural cultural property.

sights.name: Mt. Mitake
sights.description: 479-meter Shugendo mountain in northern Tsushima, once thought the highest, and home to the Tsushima leopard cat.

sights.name: Karasu Giant Sago Palm
sights.description: Tsushima's finest sago palm, about 4 meters tall and 9 meters across, designated a prefectural natural monument in 1978.

sights.name: Neso Kofun Group
sights.description: Fifth- to sixth-century mound group on a Kechiura peninsula, including three keyhole tombs.

sights.name: Idezuka Kofun (Tsurunoyama Kofun)
sights.description: Nagasaki's only front-square rear-square tomb, about 40 meters long and Tsushima's oldest.

sights.name: Dejogu-yama Burial Mound
sights.description: Unlooted stone-slab coffin on Dejogu Mountain, excavated in 1950, yielding a mirror, pottery, and beads.

sights.name: Matsumura Yasugoro and Yoshino Kazunosuke Monument
sights.description: 1861 Ofunakoshi monument to Matsumura, shot dead, and Yoshino, who died after capture.

sights.name: Takuzudama Shrine
sights.description: Historic center of Tendo faith, restored as a shrine under Meiji policy and still using the former Kannon hall.

sights.name: Kizaka Observatory
sights.description: Observatory at a trail's end, with a 180-degree east-coast view and Korean islands on clear days.

sights.name: Tazuruhara Park (Tsushima Strait Victims Memorial)
sights.description: Park with a 1992 monument consoling shipwreck victims whose remains drifted ashore on Tsushima.

sights.name: Yatateyama Burial Mounds
sights.description: Two stepped tombs on the Sasu River right bank, with corridor chambers, gilt-bronze swords, and Sue pottery.

sights.name: Nokowaki Rock
sights.description: Collapse-formed quartz-porphyry rock rising over 40 meters, best viewed from the sea.

sights.name: Amenomori Hoshu Memorial Monument
sights.description: Monument to Confucian Amenomori Hoshu, who served Tsushima from 1689 and advanced Chinese and Korean language study.

sights.name: Tomb of Haji no Uneme
sights.description: Grave of Haji no Uneme, honored in 768 for remaining faithful after widowhood and mourning her father.

sights.name: Kofunosae Site
sights.description: Kofun-period cemetery yielding Japanese and Korean pottery that shows exchange; finds shown at Kamitsushima center.

sights.name: Taterayama Foothills Nature Park Center
sights.description: Nature park office with plant and animal models, panels, and materials on Tsushima specialties and culture.

sights.name: Hokyoin-to and Gorinto Cluster
sights.description: A 2.5 m granite pagoda unmatched in the prefecture, near five-ring pagodas one dated 1374. City tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Hosei-ji Temple (Odozuka)
sights.description: Holds Tsushima's only Thousand-armed Kannon, about 170 cm, late Heian cypress, plus 14 Heian wooden Buddhas.

sights.name: Bijozuka
sights.description: Stone monument in Tsutsu telling of Tsuruo, who took her life rather than leave her mother for the capital.

sights.name: Ikazuchinomikoto Shrine
sights.description: Shrine to water god Ikazuchinomikoto, where divine-marriage rituals are still solemnly performed.

sights.name: Ikeda Beach (Ikeda Embankment)
sights.description: Stone embankment at Ikeda Beach, built under mason Masuda Sadashichi to reclaim a former pond as rice fields.

sights.name: Okubizuka
sights.description: Mound said to hold the head of So Sukekuni, killed fighting Mongols in 1274. City-designated historic site.
